components.$comment: Ordinary traversable floor beside the southern strip. This lane keeps the deleted band's lattice and phase. Its north edge stops 853 mm short of the southernmost machine, so it does not tile beneath a machine.

stitch.$comment: The floor strip connects to its adjacent traversable lane.

components.$comment: The band's own lattice at its own phase, so no cell that survives moves a step. It runs from easyloop 1 to easyloop 2 and stops dead at each: the floor between the machines is what the site needs and the floor under them is what it does not, which is the whole of the 2026-09-04 ruling.

floor_drive.$comment: The directive states no turn times, and the simulator needs none: it keeps DFW6's VTMs in their aisles.

lift.$comment: The directive gives one VTM speed and acceleration; the simulator applies them to the lift as well, which is still to be confirmed.

body.$comment: The K50-L-E1 (inventory tote carrier) column of the Ranger Relay Profile Matrix as transcribed on equipment/world-protocol-0.8, its lengths read as tenths of a millimetre.

floor_drive.$comment: The draft catalog records that 4.0 m/s and 1.8 m/s² hold only on a floor with a friction coefficient of at least 0.45 and flatness within ±3 mm per 2.25 m², and that HAI's manual derates the robot below that.

lift.$comment: The directive's four rows: 'lift, min to max', 'lift, min to cantilever height 1', 'lower, max to min' and 'lower, to cantilever height 1', which does not say from where. The height names are the rows' own; their heights, and which station handoff happens at which, are not stated (meaning unverified).

end_effector.$comment: The draft catalog describes the K50H as a comb-type platform.

body.$comment: The C56-S-2D column of the Ranger Relay Profile Matrix as transcribed on equipment/world-protocol-0.8, its lengths read as tenths of a millimetre. Its height is customisable from 2 m to 7 m, and DFW6's build is not stated.

floor_drive.$comment: The directive states no turn times, and the simulator needs none: it keeps DFW6's VTMs in their aisles.

lift.$comment: The directive gives one VTM speed and acceleration; the simulator applies them to the lift as well, which is still to be confirmed.

frame.$comment: DWG block coordinates in 0.1 mm steps. Reflection places the machine; order circulation also reverses locally so physical entries remain on the left.

region.$comment: In the FLOOR frame, not the machine's own, because that is the statement that survives a mirrored insert: a region is min-corner anchored, and a rectangle written in a mirrored frame comes out with its origin on the east edge.

go.easyloop.$comment: The machine IS this entity: its members are the cells posed in its frame, which is a stated join and not a shared identity prefix. The belt is a timing abstraction on the machine rather than on either half of it -- one L-shaped twin conveyor carries every tote both pick places work.
